analysis.description: The paper proposes Visual Concept Reasoning Networks (VCRNet), a modularized multi-branch architecture that combines a split-transform-merge strategy with attention and graph-based interaction modules to enable high-level visual concept reasoning. The model improves performance on visual recognition tasks by efficiently capturing the global context with minimal increase in parameters.

type.justification: The paper conducts experiments on various visual recognition tasks such as image classification, object detection/segmentation, scene recognition, and action recognition with large-scale datasets.
type.quote: The experimental results shows that it consistently outperforms other baseline models on multiple visual recognition tasks and only increases the number of parameters by less than 1%.
